title: SPCF 2.0 — Classification Structure
purpose: Defines the generic SPCF 2.0 classification structure and its independent catalogs.
purpose_ru: Описывает универсальную структуру классификации SPCF 2.0 и независимые справочники.

levels.name: Application Domain
levels.description: The broad domain in which the project operates: business, engineering, science, IT, and other areas.
levels.description_ru: Широкая предметная область, в которой существует проект: бизнес, инженерия, наука, ИТ и другие области.

levels.name: Activity Subdomain
levels.description: A function, process, discipline, or area of activity within an application domain.
levels.description_ru: Функция, процесс, дисциплина или направление деятельности внутри предметной области.

levels.name: Problem Domain
levels.description: A problem, constraint, unmet need, or challenge addressed by the project.
levels.description_ru: Проблема, ограничение, неудовлетворённая потребность или вызов, на который направлен проект.

levels.name: Solution Archetype
levels.description: The functional class of the project outcome; may be software, a tool, platform, methodology, standard, research artifact, or another type of result.
levels.description_ru: Функциональный класс результата проекта: программная система, инструмент, платформа, методология, стандарт, исследовательский артефакт или иной результат.

relationships.description: Conceptual many-to-many relationship; assignments are made according to the classification rules.
Conceptual many-to-many relationship; assignments are made according to the classification rules.
Conceptual many-to-many relationship; assignments are made according to the classification rules.

project_assignment.primary_secondary: A project may have multiple values at each level; primary and secondary assignments may be distinguished.
project_assignment.evidence: Project assignments are examples only; the taxonomy does not depend on any external project registry.

independent_catalogs.name: Technology Patterns
independent_catalogs.role: Implementation patterns, methods, and protocols. Not a classification level; for example, RAG belongs here, not in L4.

project_records.description: Wholly fictional e-commerce examples for demonstrating classification; no real project registry data is included.

design_principles: L1-L4 classify the meaning and purpose of a project, not its technology stack.
L2 describes an activity or discipline, not an application, team, or technology.
L3 describes the problem, not the expected benefit or outcome.
L4 describes the functional class of the result, not the stack, architecture, or deployment model.
Technologies and technology patterns remain separate from L1-L4.
Examples are fictional and demonstrate how the taxonomy can be applied; they are not source data or evidence for taxonomy relationships.
